conflicts.point: Whether open-weight models spread instantly across global networks upon release, rendering ex-ante licensing gates unenforceable.

positions.stance: Open-weight models replicate instantly across peer-to-peer networks, making upstream compliance and licensing gates technically impossible to enforce.
Commercial laboratories control the vast majority of frontier computational output and initial distribution, leaving viable enforcement points at initial commercial release.

conflicts.point: Whether statutory duty-of-care mechanisms must attach to initial commercial distribution checkpoints to compel behavioral bounds verification.

positions.stance: Statutory duty-of-care rules must attach to initial commercial release points to prevent unverified frontier systems from externalizing systemic risks.
Upstream statutory duties create prohibitive compliance costs that consolidate market power in corporate monopolies and destroy open-source innovation.

verdicts.conflict: Whether open-weight models spread instantly across global networks upon release, rendering ex-ante licensing gates unenforceable.
verdicts.rationale: Commercial laboratories currently control the vast majority of frontier computational output and initial distribution infrastructure. This concentration of compute hardware provides viable enforcement points for regulators at initial commercial release before peer-to-peer distribution occurs.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical documentation of decentralized clusters training and releasing frontier-class models entirely outside corporate laboratories.

verdicts.conflict: Whether statutory duty-of-care mechanisms must attach to initial commercial distribution checkpoints to compel behavioral bounds verification.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position accounts for systemic risk externalization by requiring verification at initial commercial release. The accelerationist claim regarding market consolidation relies on assertions of prohibitive compliance costs rather than demonstrated statutory failures.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Rigorous cost-benefit data showing that compliance mandates shutter more than fifty percent of independent AI developers.
